sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and imports
sections.what: Loads the links, state tool, media slots, graph, code explorer link, pixel image, data helpers, hover check, and mode.

sections.name: Section
sections.title: Section wrapper
sections.what: A reusable wrapper that places a numbered title beside its content on a wide screen.
sections.why: Gives every block the same look.

sections.name: ProjectDetail (part 1)
sections.title: Project header and cover setup
sections.what: Loads the project and its media, sets up the cover reveal state, builds the overview text and architecture steps, and draws the header with category, status, and links.
sections.why: Mode decides whether the overview is plain or technical.
sections.watch_out: The project lookup assumes the slug exists.

sections.name: ProjectDetail (part 2)
sections.title: Cover image and system block
sections.what: Shows the cover image, with a tap reveal on devices without hover, and the system description with its tags.
sections.why: The cover can be revealed by tap on touch screens.
sections.watch_out: The tap layer appears only on devices without hover.

sections.name: ProjectDetail (part 3)
sections.title: Architecture, screenshots, diagram, and demo
sections.what: Shows architecture steps and notes when present, screenshots in a varied grid, the stack diagram, and the demo video.
sections.why: Each section is hidden when its content is empty.
sections.watch_out: Section numbers are assigned in order, so adding or removing a section renumbers the rest.

sections.name: ProjectDetail (part 4)
sections.title: Related projects and page navigation
sections.what: Lists related projects and a footer that links back to work and forward to the next project.
sections.watch_out: The next project wraps around to the first one at the end of the list.

summary: The full page for one project: header, cover image, overview, system, architecture steps, screenshots, stack diagram, demo video, related projects, and a link to the next project.
purpose: The page a visitor sees when they open a project.
why: Puts all project information in one place and hides any section with no content.
how: Loads the project and its media by slug, then builds each section in order. Sections are numbered automatically. Empty sections are skipped.
inputs: A project slug, the project and media data, and the current mode.
outputs: A complete project article with links to the live demo, repository, code explorer, and other projects.
risks: Looking up an unknown slug uses a non-null assertion, so the page will crash. Section numbers depend on order.
debug: If the page crashes, check that the slug exists in the project data. If a section is missing, check whether its data is empty. If numbering is off, check the order of the sections.
